newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goodman makes new pitch for N.Z. assets.
newsitem.headline: Goodman makes new pitch for N.Z. assets.

text.p: Food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Friday that it had submitted a new application to the New Zealand Commerce Commission to acquire the New Zealand baking and milling assets of Defiance Mills Ltd.
Goodman said it would sell its Champion flour mill in Christchurch to a unit of George Weston Foods Ltd if the Commission approved the new application.
Goodman said the sale of the Champion mill was aimed at meeting Commerce Commission concerns about the scale of the combined business.

"We are reluctant to sell an excellent operation such as the Champion mill in Christchurch but we needed to meet Commerce Commission concerns expressed last month," Goodman chief executive David Hearn said.

The Commerce Commission said on April 14 that it rejected the NZ$48 million (A$43.2 million) bid by Goodman to buy the Defiance assets due to the potential for Goodman to become a dominant force in N.Z. markets.
A Goodman spokesman said he could not say how much George Weston would pay for the Christchurch mill as the deal was subject to a confidentiality agreement.
He said Goodman was the largest miller in New Zealand followed by the George Weston unit Allied Foods and then Defiance Mills.
George Weston is 78 percent owned by Associated British Foods Plc.

The plan to sell the Defiance assets in New Zealand coincided with a takeover bid for Defiance by South American food group Bunge, which took control of the Queensland-based company on May 16 after raising its bid a number of times.
